newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with crude, firm gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with crude, firm gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Friday in sluggish trade, underpinned by a stable crude market and reports of renewed strength in natural gas, industry sources said.

"There's been very little prompt demand, but as soon as we see some utilities out buying, resid should move up," said one cash trader, adding he would not short resid now with the cooling season ahead and fuel prices competitive with natgas.
New York Harbor physical one percent was little changed at about $14.75 a barrel, with a May 1-10 seller reported at $14.50. NYH May paper was quoted steady at $14.50-65.
NYH June one percent paper reportedly sold early at $14.75, then was quoted later at $14.80-95.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was the day's big loser, sliding 40 cents to $15.75-16.00, pressured by reports of first-half May sellers in the $15.50 area.
High sulphurs in New York again held steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $14.25-50, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices also were stable, with one percent still at $14.25-50 and three percent at $13.00-25.

New York city gate weekend gas prices gained more than five cents Friday to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent, with May quoted at about the same level. Swing gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed five cents to the $2.15/mmBtu area, or $13.55 a barrel. May gas at the Hub was quoted at about even to April.
